title: Odile and the Static
premise: Oscar Fairweather, an insurance investigator who documents the slow, unclaimed decay of the colony world Meridian's Reach, is the only witness when gravity across the entire system stutters for nine seconds. The flicker was no accident: it was a failed weapons test by the Meridian fleet, and if the rival Halcyon fleet learns of it, their fragile truce shatters into war that will erase the forgotten colony for good. To survive, Oscar must fabricate and maintain an elaborate lie — a false chain of evidence pinning the flicker on a third party — while the truce clock runs down and her own records become the most dangerous object in the system. In the end she chooses to burn her archive and broadcast the truth to both fleets at once, gambling that shared knowledge of near-catastrophe will hold the peace; it does, but only because she surrenders herself to face justice outside any law, becoming the price of two fleets' survival.
about_author: A. M. Villalobos is the pen name of a former maritime claims adjuster who spent eleven years investigating losses at sea before turning to fiction about people who document disasters for a living. They write from a converted lighthouse keeper's cottage on the Atlantic coast.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Collapses
chapters.summary: Oscar Fairweather arrives on Meridian's Reach to close out a twenty-year-old insurance file nobody expects to collect on. Through her POV we see the colony's slow rot: failing air scrubbers, abandoned children's schools, residents bartering in salvage. Emotional beat: weary professionalism masking a growing attachment to a place officially written off as a loss.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. While recording testimony in a decommissioned foundry, gravity across the whole system fails for exactly nine seconds — tools drift, rivers lift, then everything slams down. Her recorder captures the event perfectly. Emotional beat: terror giving way to the investigator's cold instinct: this was engineered, and she is holding the evidence.

chapters.title: Claims Adjuster, Adjusted
chapters.summary: Oscar reviews her footage and finds impossible physics: the flicker originated from Meridian's own orbital defense grid. A Meridian fleet liaison, Commander Ilsa Reyes, arrives asking politely for all recordings. POV alternates between Oscar and Reyes, who knows more than she says. Emotional beat: the first tightening of the trap — courtesy as coercion.

chapters.title: What the Colony Remembers
chapters.summary: Oscar interviews colonists who experienced the flicker differently — some felt pulled upward, one old engineer swears he heard a countdown. POV shifts to Tam Okafor, a teenage scavenger who found a scorched control module in the wreckage fields. Emotional beat: the forgotten colony revealing it has been keeping its own records all along.

chapters.title: The Truce Clock
chapters.summary: Reyes reveals the stakes under seal: the Meridian fleet tested a gravity weapon without authorization, and the Halcyon fleet's sensors caught the anomaly. Their truce expires in forty days. If Halcyon confirms Meridian's guilt, war follows — and Meridian's Reach sits directly in the firing line. Oscar's POV. Emotional beat: dawning horror that her insurance file could kill everyone she's met.

chapters.title: A Lie Worth Building
chapters.summary: Reyes proposes the unthinkable: manufacture evidence blaming a rogue mining consortium for the flicker. Oscar refuses — then discovers Halcyon investigators are already inbound, and her authentic recordings would damn the colony faster than any lie. She agrees, hating herself. Emotional beat: the corruption of a truth-teller, told with clinical self-disgust in her POV.

chapters.title: Forging the Impossible
chapters.summary: Oscar works with Tam and the old engineer, Adeyemi, to fabricate plausible debris and sensor ghosts implicating the consortium. POV rotates among the three as they argue ethics over soldering irons. Emotional beat: strange camaraderie forming among conspirators, undercut by Oscar's awareness that she is doing to the consortium what insurers did to this colony.

chapters.title: Halcyon Arrives
chapters.summary: Halcyon investigator Davor Kest lands with a warrant and a reputation for never being deceived. His first interview with Oscar is a duel disguised as small talk; he notices her recorder's timestamp anomalies within minutes. Alternating POV. Emotional beat: electric dread — the hunter is better than advertised, and he enjoys the hunt.

chapters.title: The Consortium Denies Everything
chapters.summary: Kest interrogates actual consortium survivors of a decades-old accident, whose genuine grief accidentally corroborates parts of Oscar's forgery. Oscar watches innocent people absorb suspicion meant for fleets. Her POV. Emotional beat: guilt crystallizing — she has chosen which innocents to sacrifice, and they look like the colonists she came to save.

chapters.title: Tam's Discovery
chapters.summary: Tam Okafor's POV. Scavenging deeper into the wreckage fields, Tam finds the weapon test's black box — real proof of Meridian's guilt — and hides it, sensing its value. Emotional beat: a child of the forgotten colony realizing she holds power over two fleets, and feeling, for the first time, like she belongs to something bigger than salvage.

chapters.title: Two Liars, One Room
chapters.summary: Kest corners Oscar privately: he knows the consortium evidence is forged, but offers to bury his finding if she helps him prove Meridian's guilt — he serves justice, not Halcyon. Oscar must decide whether the enemy investigator is her best ally. Her POV. Emotional beat: reluctant recognition of a kindred obsessive, and the terrifying relief of not being alone in the lie.

chapters.title: The Middle Passage of Evidence
chapters.summary: Oscar and Kest secretly compare notes; together they reconstruct the nine seconds with terrible precision, confirming the weapon nearly collapsed Meridian's Reach itself. Reyes discovers their collaboration. Alternating POV. Emotional beat: betrayal looming — the truce lie Oscar built is now the only thing standing between two fleets, and it is cracking.

chapters.title: Reyes Makes It Personal
chapters.summary: Reyes threatens to have Oscar's insurance license revoked, her records seized, and Tam's family deported to a labor station unless Oscar delivers Kest's findings and disappears. Oscar's POV. Emotional beat: cold fury replacing fear — the fleet has shown her exactly what kind of justice it practices, and it sounds like the insurance industry she fled.

chapters.title: What Belonging Costs
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam tries to trade the black box to Reyes for protection, but overhears Reyes planning to erase the colony's claim history entirely — Meridian's Reach will be struck from every ledger. Emotional beat: heartbreak and hardening; the girl who wanted to belong realizes belonging was always being sold to her at someone else's price.

chapters.title: Twenty-Nine Days
chapters.summary: With the truce expiring, both fleets maneuver into blockade positions around the colony. Oscar, Kest, Tam, and Adeyemi form an uneasy cell aboard a derelict tug, planning to broadcast the truth to both fleets simultaneously. Rotating POV. Emotional beat: fugitive warmth — four people with nothing left to lose building something honest out of stolen parts.

chapters.title: The Broadcast That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Their first transmission attempt is hijacked by Reyes, who broadcasts a doctored version framing Halcyon for sabotage. Both fleets go to alert status. Oscar realizes the lie has escaped everyone's control. Her POV. Emotional beat: despair at seeing her craft — fabrication — turned against her, and the understanding that only the complete truth can outrun it.

chapters.title: Black Box, Open Hand
chapters.summary: Tam surrenders the black box to Oscar voluntarily, saying the colony deserves witnesses, not owners. Kest decrypts it: full proof of the unauthorized test, including that Meridian command knew civilians were in the blast radius. Alternating POV. Emotional beat: solemnity — the truth is finally whole, and it is heavy enough to break the truce or save it, depending on how it lands.

chapters.title: Fleetfall
chapters.summary: Both fleets' vanguard squadrons engage in a skirmish above the colony; the first deaths of the war happen in sight of Meridian's Reach. Oscar watches from the ground, her archive in hand. Her POV. Emotional beat: grief and resolve fusing — every hour of hesitation now costs lives she can name.

chapters.title: The Nine-Second Truth
chapters.summary: Climax begins: Oscar hijacks the colony's ancient planetary broadcast array — the same infrastructure from chapter one — to transmit the raw black box data, her original recordings, and her signed confession of the forgery, to both fleets at once. Kest covers her against Reyes's strike team. Her POV. Emotional beat: transcendence through surrender; the investigator becomes the evidence.

chapters.title: Ceasefire at Meridian's Reach
chapters.summary: Both fleets receive identical truth simultaneously; neither can claim advantage or innocence. War councils stall, then stand down as public crews — many colonist-born — refuse to fight over a buried crime. Reyes is arrested by her own officers. Alternating POV. Emotional beat: exhausted, disbelieving relief; the truce holds not by law but by shared shame.

chapters.title: The Price, Paid
chapters.summary: Oscar surrenders to a joint tribunal for her forgery, accepting judgment outside either fleet's jurisdiction — the colony itself convenes it, its first act of self-governance in a generation. Tam and Adeyemi testify for her. Her POV. Emotional beat: bittersweet accountability; justice is imperfect, local, and finally hers to face.

chapters.title: Recertified
chapters.summary: Epilogue. Sentenced to serve as the colony's official recorder of record, Oscar opens a new ledger — not of losses, but of what Meridian's Reach rebuilds. Tam apprentices beside her; Kest sends reports from a demilitarized frontier. Final image: gravity steady, a river running normally, a child's school reopening. Emotional beat: quiet hope — survival was expensive, and it was worth every coin.
